<thought>Based on the molecular formula (C₁₄H₁₂ClO₆), the NMR data (one carbonyl at ~166 ppm, a methoxy carbon at ~61 ppm, a methyl carbon at ~14 ppm, and 11 aromatic carbons), and the presence of a chlorine atom, the most plausible way to view the structure is as two aromatic fragments that can be joined through an ester linkage. One fragment contains the chlorine and a phenolic OH attached to a benzoyl ester; the other fragment is a methoxy‑hydroxy phenyl ring. Their SMILES are:

1. O=C(Oc1c(Cl)ccc(O)c1)  – chlorinated aromatic benzoyl‑ester fragment  
2. COc1ccc(O)cc1       – methoxy‑hydroxy aromatic fragment

These two fragments together account for all atoms (C₁₄H₁₂ClO₆) and satisfy the spectroscopic information.</thought>
<final_answer>['O=C(Oc1c(Cl)ccc(O)c1)', 'COc1ccc(O)cc1']</final_answer>
